item.title: About Me
item.description:
I’m Kiet Vu, currently a Master’s student at MIT building an ultrasound kit gearing toward educational purpose. My interests are in electronics, controls & instrumentation, and design of electromechanical systems. My dream is to create new inventions, and toward that goal I am trying to learn and acquire new skills so I can expand my toolkits and be able to draw ideas from many different sources.

I was also an undergraduate at MIT in the Mechanical Engineering department (Class of 2023). Before starting my master program, I worked for a year in the system engineering role at NASA GSFC as a contractor for the Roman Space Telescope project, performing and assisting with mechanical jitter and thermal distortion analysis.

item.title: Publications
item.description:
Here’s a collection of my works with MIT & NASA GSFC that have publications or some other forms of public presence.

==========================================================

NASA/Aerodyne

  • My work at NASA GSFC / Aerodyne is primarily with the Roman Space Telescope’s Integrated Modelling Team (RST IM), where I assist with mechanical jitter testing and analysis for RST, as well as developing internal tools support our analysis process. There are great cares that go into to making sure mechanical jitters and thermal distortion effects are well-managed and understood, all with the goal of ensuring sufficient optical performance for the space telescope. Here are some of the publicly available publications that give an overview into what this process looks like:

Systems Design and Analysis of the Roman Space Telescope

K. -C. A. Liu et al., “Achieving Stability – Systems Design and Analysis of the Roman Space Telescope,” 2025 IEEE Aerospace Conference, Big Sky, MT, USA, 2025, pp. 1-17, doi: 10.1109/AERO63441.2025.11068696.
